issues.legal_issue: The constitutional market-value guarantee for compulsory acquisition of personally cultivated land applies only when a ceiling limit is prescribed by a law that was in force at the time of acquisition.
material_facts: The State appealed a High Court decision invalidating amended ceiling provisions.
The amended provisions extinguished interests in surplus land and vested that land in the State, while providing compensation based on fair and equitable rent rather than market value.
An earlier chapter prescribing a ceiling limit had never been brought into operation by notification and was repealed before the amended provisions were applied.
The landholders relied on the earlier chapter as establishing a ceiling limit applicable to their personally cultivated land.
issues.conclusion: The earlier chapter did not establish a ceiling limit under a law in force, so the second proviso to Article 31-A did not require market-value compensation for the landholders’ land; the amended chapter was not invalid on that ground, and the appeals were allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the second proviso to Article 31-A, market-value compensation is guaranteed for compulsory acquisition of personally cultivated land only to the extent that the land falls within a ceiling limit applicable under a law for the time being in force. A provision that has not been brought into operation by legislative enactment or by an authorized delegate is not in force merely because it has been enacted or could have been commenced. The Court distinguished A. Thangal Kunju Mudaliar v. M. Venkitachalam Potti, [1955] 2 S.C.R. 1196: that case treated the provision empowering a successor government to commence a statute as an existing law, but did not hold that the statute’s uncommenced substantive provisions were already in force. The Court also considered Articles 31(2) and 31(2A) in identifying the vesting of land in the State as compulsory acquisition.

predicates.state_appeal_from_invalidity_ruling: The State appealed a ruling that invalidated amended land-ceiling provisions.
predicates.state_acquires_personally_cultivated_est: The challenged provisions provide for the State to acquire land held under personal cultivation in an estate.
predicates.prior_ceiling_limit_never_operated: An earlier rule prescribing a ceiling limit was never brought into operation by the authority empowered to commence it.
predicates.prior_ceiling_rule_repealed_before_acqui: The earlier rule prescribing a ceiling limit was repealed before the challenged acquisition provisions were applied.
predicates.amended_ceiling_compensation_law_not_inv: The amended ceiling and compensation law is not invalid for failing to provide market-value compensation under the constitutional guarantee.

issues.definition: When the State appeals a ruling invalidating acquisition provisions, the land is personally cultivated estate land, and the earlier ceiling rule was never operated and was repealed before acquisition, the amended law is not invalid under the market-value guarantee.
